new_candidates.body:
### Describe the bug

`MultiDiscrete` accepts a starting value and count whose largest element cannot be represented by the selected integer dtype. Sampling then wraps around and returns values outside the intended discrete range; the space can reject its own samples.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
from gymnasium.spaces import MultiDiscrete

space = MultiDiscrete([4], start=[126], dtype=np.int8, seed=0)
sample = space.sample()
print(sample)                 # [-128], instead of a value in 126..129
print(space.contains(sample)) # False
```

Likewise, `MultiDiscrete([3], start=[254], dtype=np.uint8)` can produce 0. The valid mathematical ranges extend beyond 127 / 255 respectively, so the constructor should reject them rather than silently create an unrepresentable space.

### Expected behavior and fix

Raise `ValueError` for unrepresentable upper endpoints. Valid spaces, including negative starts, exact dtype maxima and large uint64 starts, must remain unchanged. A validated fix and regression tests are provided in the linked PR.

The constructor can check `start > dtype_max - (nvec - 1)` after count positivity. The subtraction stays representable and avoids evaluating an overflowing upper endpoint. This is separate from #1622 (membership checks on valid spaces), #1737 (masked sampling) and #1739 (flattening).

### Evidence

Current main `57c1610`, Gymnasium 1.4.0, Linux / Python 3.11.17. New final regressions on unchanged code: 7 failed, 9 passed; patched MultiDiscrete tests: 38 passed; full spaces suite: 1615 passed. Full pre-commit passed. Whole-project pytest is blocked at collection by optional MoviePy, including on unchanged code; no full-suite pass is claimed.

AI disclosure: Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Codex assisted investigation, implementation and testing; no independent human review is claimed.

Fix and complete regression coverage: https://github.com/Farama-Foundation/Gymnasium/pull/1790
